Francis Scott Key Bridge Update:
 
This morning, President Biden convened senior members of his team for a briefing on the ongoing response to the collapse of the Francis Scott Key Bridge.

During the briefing, President Biden directed his team to ensure all federal resources be made available to assist in the ongoing search and rescue efforts and response to this incident.

Francis Scott Key Bridge Update:
 
This morning, President Biden convened senior members of his team for a briefing on the ongoing response to the collapse of the Francis Scott Key Bridge.

During the briefing, President Biden directed his team to ensure all federal resources be made available to assist in the ongoing search and rescue efforts and response to this incident.

media.alt_text: President Biden is briefed on the collapse of the Francis Scott Key Bridge.

tweets.text: President Biden also spoke with Governor Moore, Mayor Scott, County Executive Olszewski, both U.S. Senators, the Congressman, and Secretary Buttigieg. He told them we will send any federal resource they need as we respond to this emergency and rebuild together.

tweets.text: The U.S. Coast Guard is leading the response at the port, where representatives from the Federal Highway Administration, the FBI, the Department of Transportation, and the Army Corps of Engineers – as well as Maryland officials and Baltimore Police and Fire – are working together to coordinate the emergency response.

On the 14th anniversary of the signing of the Affordable Care Act, the results are clear.
 
Under President Biden, more Americans have health insurance than under any President.

21 million Americans signed up for health coverage this year
- That includes 1.7 million Black Americans and 3.4 million Latino Americans
- A majority of shoppers found coverage for less than $10 a month

President Biden is not resting on his accomplishments, he has a bold agenda to continue to bring down Americans’ health care costs.
- Calling on Congress to make expanded Affordable Care Act tax credits permanent
- Lowering prescription drug prices
- Fighting to increase the number of drugs Medicare can negotiate on for lower prices
- Working to expand $35 a month insulin and a $2,000 out of pocket cap on drug spending to everyone

And despite Republican elected officials fighting to get rid of the Affordable Care Act – President Biden has been clear:
 
He will always protect and strengthen the Affordable Care Act, Medicare, and Medicaid.
